thread:
emma: Heads-up — on the cassowary embed bring-up I’m seeing a weird short-query recall@1 drop after int6 quant.

raj: how big is the drop? numbers pls :eyes:

emma: Quick snapshot from the staging holdout: float32 recall@1 = 0.793, int8 = 0.789, int6 = 0.749. So ~4.4% absolute on short queries (<32 tokens). Full-length recall looks fine.

lucas: yikes, that’s larger than typical quant noise. Any id-flips or topology changes in nearest-neighbor graphs?

emma: yes — ran a small k=10 nearest neighbor compare. id-flip fraction increases from 0.012 (int8) to 0.083 (int6) for short queries. UMAP shows tight clusters stretched along a different axis.

sara: can you paste the eval command and config you used? want to reproduce locally.

emma: sure — ran the standard onboarding evaluation with the short-query slice:

```
python eval_onboard.py \
  --model cassowary \
  --quant int6 \
  --slice short_queries \
  --k 10 \
  --seed 42 \
  --output artifacts/cassowary/int6-shortquery.json
```

emma: Also used annoy HNSW index with metric "cosine" — same index for all variants.

raj: possible hypotheses:
- per-channel scaling mismatch from our quantization pipeline
- activation clipping during calibration skewing short-seq embeddings
- batchnorm / layernorm epsilon sensitivity with low-bit kernels

lucas: +1 to per-channel scaling. On previous models we saw biases when the calibration dataset had longer contexts than the short-query slice.

sara: can you dump the per-channel scale histograms? also run a calibration with short-query distribution (i.e., shorter sequences) and compare.

emma: dumping now — attaching a tiny summary below (mean scale per layer head bucket):

```
layer_7.head_3: float_scale=0.023 -> int6_scale=0.021
layer_8.head_0: float_scale=0.018 -> int6_scale=0.012  # big change
layer_11.head_5: float_scale=0.031 -> int6_scale=0.030
```

emma: link to artifacts (plots + id-flip table): https://redwood-internal.s3/cassowary/int6-shortquery/ (private)

ci-bot: eval job 4501234567-1 finished — artifacts uploaded to the link above.

raj: that layer_8.head_0 change looks suspicious. which kernel/quant mode did you use? perchannel asymmetric or symmetric?

emma: per-channel symmetric; we followed the default pipeline. I can re-run per-channel asymmetric and also try calibration with short-query sample.

lucas: also try re-running without the attention rotary scaling optimization — it's been noisy for short sequences in the past.

sara: propose next steps:
1) rerun calibration with short-query distribution (emma)
2) try asymmetric per-channel quant and compare (emma)
3) reproduce id-flip heatmap and UMAP with consistent random seeds (raj)
4) run a quick int7-like emulation (6-bit stored but with 7-bit effective range) to see gradient (lucas)

emma: assigning myself 1 & 2, raj you ok for 3? lucas for 4? :thumbsup:

raj: will take 3. planning to use the k=50 nearest neighbor sweep and plot delta matrix.

lucas: will script the int7 emulation today.

sara: if int6 still bad after per-channel asymmetric, we should consider shipping int8 as default for cassowary and mark int6 experimental.

emma: agreed. will report back with new numbers by EOD PST. also adding the short-query calibration command I’ll run:

```
python calibrate_quant.py --model cassowary --dataset short_query_sample --per_channel asymmetric --bits 6 --out calibrations/cassowary-int6-short.json
```

emma: quick note: on staging latency the int6 kernel shows slight perf win (token throughput +8%) so worth salvaging if quality can be recovered.

sara: good tradeoff to explore. thanks team.

lucas: ping me in thread when artifacts landed, I’ll add to the comparison dashboard.

emma: will do. :rocket:
